english_after: For by the grace given to me I say to everyone among you: Do not think more highly than you should, but think with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given each of you.

english_before: For as in one body we have many members, but all the members have not the same office:
english_after: For just as we have many members in one body, and the members do not all have the same function,

english_before: So we, being many, are one body in Christ; and everyone members one of another:
english_after: so we, though many, are one body in Christ, and individually we are members of one another.

english_before: And having different gifts, according to the grace that is given us, either prophecy, to be used according to the rule of faith;
english_after: We have different gifts according to the grace given us. If the gift is prophecy, use it in keeping with the faith.

english_before: Or ministry, in ministering; or he that teaches, in doctrine;
english_after: If it is service, then serve. If it is teaching, then teach.

english_before: He that exhorts, in exhorting; he that gives, with simplicity; he that rules, with carefulness; he that shows mercy, with cheerfulness.
english_after: If it is exhortation, then exhort. Let the one who gives do so with sincerity, the one who leads with diligence, and the one who shows mercy with cheerfulness.

english_before: Let love be without dissimulation. Hating that which is evil, cleaving to that which is good,
english_after: Let love be sincere. Hate what is evil and cling to what is good.

english_before: Loving one another with the love of brotherhood: with honor preventing one another.
english_after: Love one another with brotherly affection. Take the lead in honoring one another.

english_before: In carefulness not slothful. In spirit fervent. Serving the Lord.
english_after: Do not be slack in diligence. Be fervent in spirit. Serve the Lord.

english_before: Rejoicing in hope. Patient in tribulation. Instant in prayer.
english_after: Rejoice in hope. Be patient in affliction. Be steadfast in prayer.

english_before: Communicating to the necessities of the saints. Pursuing hospitality.
english_after: Share in meeting the needs of the saints. Pursue hospitality.

english_before: Bless them that persecute you: bless, and curse not.
english_after: Bless those who persecute you. Bless them and do not curse them.

english_before: Rejoice with them that rejoice: weep with them that weep.
english_after: Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.

english_before: Being of one mind one towards another. Not minding high things, but consenting to the humble. Do not be wise in your own conceits.
english_after: Be of one mind with one another. Do not set your minds on lofty things, but embrace what is humble. Do not be wise in your own eyes.

english_before: To no one rendering evil for evil. Providing good things, not only in the sight of God but also in the sight of all men.
english_after: Repay no one evil for evil. Take thought for what is good before God and before everyone.

english_before: If it be possible, as much as is in you, have peace with all men.
english_after: If possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.

english_before: Revenge not yourselves, my dearly beloved; but make room to wrath, for it is written: Revenge is mine, I will repay, says the Lord.
english_after: Beloved, do not avenge yourselves, but give place to wrath. For it is written, “Vengeance is mine. I will repay, says the Lord.”

english_before: But if your enemy be hungry, give him to eat; if he thirst, give him to drink. For, doing this, you shall heap coals of fire upon his head.
english_after: But if your enemy is hungry, feed him. If he is thirsty, give him something to drink. For by doing this you will heap burning coals on his head.

english_before: Do not be overcome by evil: but overcome evil by good.
english_after: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

english_after: If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and it will be given to him.

english_before: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavers is like a wave of the sea, which is moved and carried about by the wind.
english_after: But let him ask in faith, without wavering. For the one who wavers is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.

english_before: But let the brother of low condition glory in his exaltation:
english_after: Let the lowly brother glory in being raised up,

english_after: and let the rich man glory in being brought low, for he will pass away like a flower in the grass.

english_before: For the sun rose with a burning heat and parched the grass: and the flower of it fell off, and the beauty of the shape of it perished. So also shall the rich man fade away in his ways.

english_before: Then, when desire has conceived, it brings forth sin. But sin, when it is completed, begets death.
english_after: Then desire conceives and gives birth to sin, and sin, when it is full grown, gives birth to death.

english_after: For he chose to give us birth by the word of truth, so that we might be a kind of beginning of his creation.

english_before: Therefore, casting away all uncleanness and abundance of naughtiness, with meekness receive the ingrafted word, which is able to save your souls.
english_after: So put away all uncleanness and the abundance of evil. Receive with meekness the implanted word, which can save your souls.

english_before: For if a man be a hearer of the word and not a doer, he shall be compared to a man beholding his own countenance in a glass.
english_after: For if anyone hears the word and does not do it, he is like a man looking at his own face in a mirror.

english_before: For he saw himself and went his way and immediately forgot what manner of man he was.
english_after: He looked at himself, went away, and immediately forgot what he looked like.

english_before: But he that has looked into the perfect law of liberty and has continued in it, not becoming a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work: this man shall be blessed in his deed.

english_before: And if any man think himself to be religious, not bridling his tongue but deceiving his own heart, this man’s religion is vain.
english_after: If anyone thinks he is religious but does not bridle his tongue and deceives his own heart, his religion is empty.

english_before: Religion clean and undefiled before God and the Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their tribulation and to keep one’s self unspotted from this world.
english_after: Religion that is pure and undefiled before God the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their distress and to keep oneself unstained by this world.

english_before: Be not many masters, my brothers, knowing that you receive the greater judgment.
english_after: My brothers, let not many of you become teachers, knowing that you will receive a stricter judgment.

english_before: For in many things we all offend. If any man offend not in word, the same is a perfect man. He is able also with a bridle to lead about the whole body.
english_after: For we all stumble in many ways. If anyone does not stumble in what he says, he is a perfect man, able to bridle his whole body as well.

english_before: For if we put bits into the mouths of horses, that they may obey us: and we turn about their whole body.
english_after: When we put bits in horses’ mouths to make them obey us, we guide their whole bodies.

english_before: Behold also ships, whereas they are great and are driven by strong winds, yet are they turned about with a small helm, wherever the force of the governor wills.
english_after: Look at ships too. Though they are large and driven by strong winds, they are steered by a small rudder wherever the pilot wishes.

english_before: Even so the tongue is indeed a little member and boasts great things. Behold how small a fire kindles a great wood.
english_after: So also the tongue is a small member, yet it boasts of great things. See what a fire can set so great a forest ablaze!

english_before: And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity. The tongue is placed among our members, which defiles the whole body and inflames the wheel of our nativity, being set on fire by Gehenna.
english_after: The tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity among the parts of our body. It stains the whole body and sets the course of our life ablaze, itself set on fire by Gehenna.

english_before: For every nature of beasts and of birds and of serpents and of the rest is tamed and has been tamed, by the nature of man.
english_after: Every kind of beast, bird, serpent, and other creature is tamed and has been tamed by humankind,

english_before: But the tongue no one can tame, an unquiet evil, full of deadly poison.
english_after: but no one can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.

english_before: Out of the same mouth proceeds blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not so to be.
english_after: From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things should not be so.

english_before: Who is a wise man and endued with knowledge, among you? Let him show, by a good conversation, his work in the meekness of wisdom.
english_after: Who among you is wise and learned? Let him show his works by his good conduct, in the meekness that comes from wisdom.

english_before: But if you have bitter zeal, and there be quarrels in your hearts: glory not and do not be liars against the truth.
english_after: But if you have bitter zeal and rivalry in your hearts, do not boast and lie against the truth.

english_before: But the wisdom that is from above, first indeed is chaste, then peaceable, modest, easy to be persuaded, consenting to the good, full of mercy and good fruits, without judging, without dissimulation.
english_after: But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, modest, open to persuasion, willing to agree with what is good, full of mercy and good fruits, without judging and without pretense.

english_before: Who by faith conquered kingdoms, wrought justice, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
english_after: By faith they conquered kingdoms, practiced righteousness, obtained promises, and shut the mouths of lions,

english_after: announcing the end from the beginning and, from the outset, things not yet done. I say, “My counsel will stand, and all that I will shall come to pass.”

english_after: The Lord willed to crush him in weakness. If he gives his life for sin, he will see long-lived offspring, and the Lord’s purpose will prosper in his hand.

english_after: Blessed is the man who has not followed the counsel of the ungodly, stood on the path of sinners, or sat in the seat of pestilence,

english_after: He has settled me in a place of pasture. He has nourished me beside refreshing water;

english_after: He has restored my soul. He has led me along paths of righteousness for His name’s sake.

english_before: Wash me still more from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.
english_after: Wash me more thoroughly of my iniquity, and cleanse me of my sin.

english_before: You will give joy and gladness to my hearing, and the humbled bones will rejoice.
english_after: You will let me hear joy and gladness, and the humbled bones will rejoice.

english_before: Create a clean heart in me, God, and renew an upright spirit within my inward parts.
english_after: Create a clean heart in me, God, and renew an upright spirit deep within me.

english_before: For passing by and seeing your idols, I found an altar also, on which was written: To the Unknown God. What therefore you worship without knowing it, that I preach to you:

english_before: God, who made the world and all things in it, he being Lord of heaven and earth, dwells not in temples made with hands.
english_after: The God who made the world and everything in it is Lord of heaven and earth. He does not dwell in temples made by hand,

english_before: Neither is he served with men’s hands, as though he needed anything: seeing it is he who gives to all life and breath and all things:
english_after: nor is he served by human hands as though he needed anything. He himself gives everyone life and breath and all things.

english_before: And has made of one, all mankind, to dwell upon the whole face of the earth, determining appointed times and the limits of their habitation.
english_after: From one man he made all humankind to dwell on the whole face of the earth, and he set their appointed times and the boundaries of where they would live,

english_before: For in him we live and move and are: as some also of your own poets said: For we are also his offspring.
english_after: For in him we live and move and have our being, as some of your own poets have said, ‘For we too are his offspring.’

english_before: And God indeed having winked at the times of this ignorance, now declares to men that all should everywhere repent.
english_after: God overlooked those times of ignorance, but now he announces to all people everywhere that they should repent,

english_before: Because he has appointed a day wherein he will judge the world in equity, by the man whom he has appointed: giving faith to all, by raising him up from the dead.
english_after: because he has appointed a day when he will judge the world with equity through the man he has appointed. He has given everyone assurance of this by raising him from the dead.

english_before: And when they had heard of the resurrection of the dead, some indeed mocked. But others said: We will hear you again concerning this matter.
english_after: When they heard about the resurrection of the dead, some mocked, but others said, “We will hear you again about this.”

english_after: But some men joined him and believed, among them Dionysius the Areopagite, as well as a woman named Damaris and others with them.

english_before: For why did Christ, when yet we were weak, according to the time, die for the ungodly?
english_after: For why did Christ die for the ungodly at the appointed time, while we were still weak?

english_after: For scarcely anyone dies for a righteous man, though someone might dare to die for a good man.

english_after: Christ died for us. Much more, then, now that we have been justified by his blood, will we be saved from wrath through him.

english_before: For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son: much more, being reconciled, shall we be saved by his life.
english_after: For if we were reconciled to God through the death of his Son while we were enemies, how much more, now that we are reconciled, will we be saved by his life!

english_after: For sin was in the world before the law, but sin was not counted when there was no law.

english_after: Yet death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over those who had not sinned as Adam did. He was a figure of the one to come.

english_after: But the gift is not like the offense. For if many died by the offense of one, much more did the grace of God and the gift through the grace of one man, Jesus Christ, abound to many.

english_before: And not as it was by one sin, so also is the gift. For judgment indeed was by one to condemnation: but grace is of many offences to justification.
english_after: And the gift is not like what came through one sin. For the judgment from one offense led to condemnation, but grace after many offenses led to justification.

english_after: For if death reigned through one man because of his offense, how much more will those who receive an abundance of grace, gift, and righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!

english_before: Therefore, as by the offence of one, to all men to condemnation: so also by the justice of one, to all men to justification of life.
english_after: So just as one man’s offense led to condemnation for all, so one man’s righteousness leads to justification and life for all.

english_before: For as by the disobedience of one man, many were made sinners: so also by the obedience of one, many shall be made just.
english_after: For just as many were made sinners through the disobedience of one man, so through the obedience of one man many will be made righteous.

english_before: Now the law entered in that sin might abound. And where sin abounded, grace did more abound.
english_after: The law came in so that the offense might abound. But where the offense abounded, grace abounded all the more,

english_before: That as sin has reigned to death: so also grace might reign by justice to life everlasting, through Jesus Christ our Lord.
english_after: so that just as sin reigned in death, grace too might reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
